sourceGaps: 2006T1: The question gives $0.50\ \mathrm{cm\,s^{-1}}$, while the printed key substitutes $0.51\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Its numerical energy and final Avogadro value are retained literally, without correcting the source.

2006T2: Question 2.5 says “Fill in the blank”, but the collection prints no corresponding blank reaction scheme before the solution. The printed key is retained without inventing the absent question layout. Key 2.2 labels the $656.3\ \mathrm{nm}$ transition as $2\to3$, while the question uses $3\to2$. Key 2.4 prints the numerator unit m, without /s, and that literal substitution is retained.

2006T3: The key awards full credit to both the residence-time and half-life approaches. It also accepts both the shortest-path and random-walk calculations in 3.2. Its $160$-year random-walk result exceeds the printed option (b) upper bound of $100$ years, but the key still names (b); this contradiction is retained. The printed temperature labels in the 3.3 exponent are not silently reordered.

2006T4: The question asks for any three alternative pairs, but the printed key supplies nine drawings. All nine are retained in their native arrangement, including two differently arranged thymine-thymine pairs. No alternative is omitted or treated as a new whole task.

2006T5: On physical page 601 the second neutralization reaction prints $\mathrm{H_2PO_4}$ without its negative charge. The next page's reaction and concentration table include the charge. Both literal forms are retained.

2006T6: The key's native matching diagram has four rows; the question has five, with the copper potential addressed by the surrounding prose. All are retained. In 6.5 the symbolic hydroxide factor is squared but its numerical substitution is not; the printed result remains unchanged. The question calls mAh stored “energy”; that original wording is retained. Both half-reaction normalizations and the alternative 6.6 method remain complete.

2006T7: Native physical page 608 visibly prints $\mathrm{Hg_2(g)}$ in the first 7-2 reaction, unlike the surrounding hydrogen reactions. That literal source typo is retained. In 7.1, the gas constant uses a decimal comma, rendered as $8{,}314$. The key's work values are signed negative. Its time equation equates a kJ value directly to watt-seconds without printing the unit-conversion factor; the subsequent duration is retained. The final motor-duration/current request is unnumbered in the source and stays within 7.3, rather than becoming an invented 7.4.

2006T8: Native key page 611 visibly prints $-7.4$ in its entropy substitution, while the question gives $87.40$ and the printed result is $15.36\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The extracted text layer instead reports 87.4; the original image governs this transcription. The discrepancy is retained without changing the result. Native orbital arrows, all six electrons and complete lattice edges are retained.

2006T9: Question 9.2 literally prints $\mathrm{CH_3-N}$; neighboring questions use $\mathrm{CH_3-N_3}$. The native 612 and 613 reaction images have partially obscured/broken intermediate captions; these are printed that way in the original PDF and retained. The upper 9.6 branch prints B both before and after the carbonate intermediate, whereas the key labels the alkene B and carbon dioxide C. The second branch caption is broken as “heterocycli / c” in the native figure. These discrepancies are disclosed without replacing or redrawing the schemes. All key Lewis structures, charges, lone pairs and polymer boundaries remain present.
